items.q: What did the Calendly clone do on the first prompt?
items.a: Google sign-in, weekday hours, a **15-minute booking link**, name and email checks, and a **confirmation email**. A second prompt adds edits, emoji, and a required question. He puts the saving at **$10 to $20**.

items.q: What does he count as the 80 percent of Typeform?
items.a: Build questions, change types, **collect answers**, and share. Ask has multiple choice, short text, and a **1–10 rating**. Preview and a yes/no question are one more prompt. He says form tools can run to **$400**.

items.q: What is the line between inspiration and a copy?
items.a: Write the **feature list** and ship it under your own name. Leave their **code, images, logos, and paid features** alone. Lanes got drag, covers, checklists, and an invite. A stretched cover and no save button are the leftover gaps.

items.q: When is the rebuild worth the time?
items.a: A **$200 or $1,000** monthly tool that AI can replace in **a day or two**. A **$20 to $100** tool that would take a long time, without a team of experts, is the weaker trade.

items.q: What does he say Ria actually is?
items.a: **420,000 lines** of TypeScript, with **789** pulled into the reverse-engineering skill. It reads **UI, logic, and data**. He says that path is faster than the same job in Claude or ChatGPT.
